issues.failure_explanation: Training normal equations do not impose orthogonality on independent diagnostic data or at the population level. A fitted coefficient error can lie entirely in the fitted span. For example, if the fitted predictor differs from m by a constant c, every positive-degree Legendre probe has zero population residual moment, although the excess risk is c². More generally, errors along fitted orthogonal basis functions are invisible to all higher-degree orthogonal probes. Finite-sample least squares can produce exactly these errors.

issues.failure_explanation: The population characterization requires all directions, whereas no finite plateau establishes that untested directions are negligible. With uniform X, take noiseless Y equal to a normalized Legendre polynomial of degree M beyond every inspected degree. Lower-degree population fits and probes show a perfectly stable positive residual floor, although the true aleatoric floor is zero. Moreover, small individual coefficients do not bound total L² error: an error spread equally over N orthonormal directions has unit total squared norm but per-direction effect 1/N. Completeness supplies neither a finite tail bound nor the quantitative implication used by the stop rule.

issues.failure_explanation: No entropy or integrability hypothesis makes the subtraction legitimate. With constant X, let p(y)=1/[y(log(1/y))²] on (0,e⁻¹). This is a density with H(p)=−∞. issues.failure_explanation: Averaging within snapshots addresses spatial dependence but not serial dependence between H_t values from one trajectory. Downsampling to reduce correlation does not establish independence. For serially correlated stationary moments, the variance of √T times their mean involves Γ(0)+2∑_{ℓ≥1}Γ(ℓ), whereas the proposed sample variance estimates only Γ(0). Neither an independence justification nor a valid long-run variance argument is supplied, so the nominal t_59 and Bonferroni significance calibration is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Justify negligible inter-snapshot dependence at the retained sampling interval, or replace the calibration with a temporally valid block or long-run-variance method under stated dependence assumptions. Otherwise present these t-values only descriptively.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed significance-test corroboration of the Lorenz–96 degree selection lacks its stated calibration.
issues.title: Snapshot clustering does not justify the temporal t-test calibration
issues.why_classification: Validating or replacing the dependence calibration requires a contained additional statistical analysis; the population theory and descriptive experiment can remain.
